title: This Keyboard Is So Smart, It Can Tell How Hard You're Pressing!
summary:
Imagine a keyboard that knows exactly how hard you're pressing each key. That's the magic of the Wooting 60HE v2! Instead of normal switches that click when you push them all the way down, this keyboard uses magnets and sensors. It can tell if you're pressing a key just a little bit or all the way down. Why does that matter? In games, you can set it so a light press makes your character walk, and a full press makes them sprint—all on the same key!

This keyboard is built for gamers who want every advantage. It's super fast, with an 8,000 Hz polling rate (that means it checks for key presses 8,000 times every second!). You can customize almost everything: change what each key does, adjust how sensitive they are, and even make the keyboard act like a game controller's joystick for racing games. There's a split spacebar option too, which gives your thumbs extra buttons for shortcuts.

Some people might not like that it's a small 60% keyboard (no number pad or arrow keys), but you can set up arrow keys by holding down other keys. The carrying strap on the side is removable if you think it looks silly. The keys feel smooth and quiet, and the colorful lights can be tweaked to any shade you want. It's not cheap, but for serious gamers, this keyboard is a game-changer—literally!
why_it_matters: If you play games on a computer, understanding how a fast keyboard works can help you see why equipment matters and maybe inspire you to learn about tech.

background_read: Wooting is a company from the Netherlands that makes special gaming keyboards with analog input, meaning they can detect how far a key is pressed.
Most normal keyboards check for key presses about 125 times per second, but the Wooting 60HE v2 checks 8,000 times per second, giving almost instant response.
A 60% keyboard is a smaller keyboard that removes the number pad, function row, and arrow keys to save space on a desk.
Article_Structure: WHO: Gamers who want more control and speed in their computer games
WHAT: The Wooting 60HE v2 keyboard that uses magnets and sensors to tell how hard keys are pressed and checks for presses 8,000 times per second
WHERE: On gaming computers around the world, especially for players of fast-paced or racing games
WHY: To give a competitive edge by allowing light and heavy presses to do different actions and by being extremely responsive
